analysis.title: New attacks on Iran will lead to nowhere and the cost would be high
key_insights: Brent Jan-27 rose 1.6% last week, trading $109.02-114.29/b and closing at $113.43/b. The Dec-26 contract rolled off Friday at $117.64/b. Dated Brent closed at $118.77/b.
Physical premiums for Fortis and Oseberg fell to $5.9/b and $1.9/b after reaching unusual highs of $20/b recently, a sign of softening physical crude prices.

Brent Jan-27 is down 3.3% on the morning of 2 November to $100.8/b after Trump indicated he will give diplomacy another chance. This partially erases the elevated risk premium as an imminent attack after 3 November appears averted for now.

SEB argues new US/Israeli attacks on Iran would lead nowhere politically. Gulf countries do not want another round, and the US did not consult its Gulf allies or seek support from allies other than Israel.

Iran has had about 6 months to rebuild defensive and offensive capabilities since the March-April attacks. It is assumed to hold 3/4 of its prewar ammunition and likely has a large stock of ballistic rockets.
The Gulf states and the US have used a major share of their defensive interceptors (Patriots and Thaad), so a new attack carries more risk than one in May.
Iranian media said Iran would retaliate with no geographical limitations if attacked.
Columbia's Karen Young expects a US-Israel attack, a declaration of victory and a deal favorable to Iran, which would make another attack a way to exit. SEB says it will see.
Oil faces a two-sided outcome. A new attack with Gulf energy infrastructure damage would send prices sharply higher. If no attack happens, the market faces a surplus and much lower prices.

sector_views.rationale: Two-sided risk. Infrastructure damage from a new attack would lift prices sharply, while no attack leaves a surplus and much lower oil prices.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The contract rose 1.6% on the week within a $109.02-114.29/b range.
The contract rolled off on Friday at this close.
Dated Brent stayed strong even as physical premiums fell.
Down 3.3% on the morning as Trump signalled more diplomacy, partially erasing the risk premium.

macro_indicators.indicator: Brent reversion scenario cited from Mike McGlone
macro_indicators.interpretation: McGlone argues Brent reverts to $60/b unless conditions in the Russia-Ukraine and US-Iran wars worsen.

risk_factors: A new US/Israeli attack on Iran with widespread Gulf energy infrastructure damage would send oil prices sharply higher.
Iranian retaliation without geographical limits, with Iran assumed to hold 3/4 of its prewar ammunition and a large stock of ballistic rockets.
Depleted Gulf and US interceptor stocks (Patriots and Thaad) raise the cost of a new round of hostilities.
If no attack happens, the oil market faces a surplus and much lower prices.
geopolitical: US/Israel and Iran: Trump gave diplomacy another chance and an imminent attack after 3 November appears averted for now.
Gulf states are pursuing diplomatic efforts to avert a new US/Israeli attack on Iran. None want another round.
Egypt's foreign minister Badr Abdelatty said a second round would be more dangerous, more destructive and lead nowhere.
Iran says it would retaliate without geographical limitations. Earlier US-Israeli attacks came in March and April, with briefer attacks in June and 1 September (about 10 hours).
Russia's attacks on civilians in Ukraine are cited as a parallel to the belief that force will make Iran bend.
Russia-Ukraine war conditions are cited by McGlone as relevant to Brent's path.

tension_points.bull_case: A new US/Israeli attack with widespread Gulf energy infrastructure damage would send oil prices sharply higher. Iran is assumed to hold 3/4 of its prewar ammunition and has threatened retaliation without geographical limits.
tension_points.bear_case: If the attack does not happen, the global oil market faces a surplus and much lower prices. McGlone sees reversion to $60/b without worsening conditions in the two wars.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An attack after 3 November, which SEB says appears averted for now after Trump gave diplomacy another chance.

theme_stances.key_argument: A new round of attacks on Iran will lead nowhere politically, and the risk is larger than in May.
theme_stances.evidence: We totally agree with Badr Abdlatty above: "it will lead to nowhere".
